more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Calcium iodate is an inorganic calcium salt of iodic acid. FDA describes a synthetic preparation route using iodine, lime solution and chlorine. Its specified direct-food function is dough strengthening during bread manufacture. The use limit is expressed relative to flour weight rather than as a general daily intake.
more_info.origin: FDA describes chemical preparation by passing chlorine through a heated lime solution containing iodine. The resulting calcium iodate is an inorganic salt. This is a synthesis route; the specification does not describe a plant or animal extract.
more_info.uses: Used as a dough strengthener in bread manufacture. The US regulation sets a maximum of 0.0075% relative to flour weight. The bread standard also sets a combined limit for its specified dough-conditioning group.
